Common haplotype orientation of clone states per piece (MEDICC2 export, step 2)

Source: R/medicc2.R
orient_clone_states.Rd

Per piece, a reference clone is chosen among the clones with an imbalanced state (major != minor on a diploid piece): the clone with the largest expected orientation signal a * |major / cn - 0.5| * sqrt(n), where a is the clone's allelic attenuation (clones$a, 1 when missing) and n its pooled votes on the piece. Each phase block (piece x phase set) is oriented by the sign of the reference clone's pooled votes (A - B; ties and blocks without reference votes are left unoriented and do not count). Every clone's votes on the oriented blocks are pooled into an oriented fraction f: the fraction of the reference clone's major haplotype. The convention is cn_a = the reference clone's major haplotype; a clone with an imbalanced state gets cn_a = major, cn_b = minor when f >= 0.5, else the swap. Balanced states (n:n, 0:0) and haploid pieces (male chrX, ploidy 1) pass through as cn_a = major, cn_b = minor.

Usage

orient_clone_states(
  pieces,
  features,
  assignments,
  clones = NULL,
  use = c("confident", "assigned"),
  near = 0.05,
  chain = c("parsimony", "phase", "none"),
  min_link = 50
)

Arguments

pieces

medicc2_pieces() output

features

list with votes (cell index, atom, ps, nA, nB), atoms and cells (the cells the vote index refers to: data.table with a cell column or a character vector), e.g. an scn_features object

assignments

assignments table (cell, clone and the use column)

clones

clones table (for the attenuation a); NULL = 1

use

cells pooled per clone: confident or assigned

near

half-width around 0.5 of the low-confidence flag

chain

label chaining between adjacent pieces: parsimony (phase-set fallback), phase (parsimony fallback) or none (each piece's cn_a is its reference clone's major haplotype)

min_link

minimal summed block weight (votes) of a phase-set link

Value

list of class medicc2_orientation:

  • pieces: the input rows plus n_votes (clone votes on the piece), n_oriented (on oriented blocks), f (oriented fraction of the cn_a haplotype), dev (|f - 0.5|), is_ref, swapped (cn_a = minor), cn_a, cn_b and flag (ref, ok, low_conf, no_votes, no_ref, balanced, haploid).

  • qc: one row per piece: piece, chrom, start, end, orient_ref, ref_state, ref_score, flipped (labels flipped by chaining), link (first, phase, parsimony, none), link_score (phase: weighted sign agreement between -1 and 1 before the flip; parsimony: the weighted direction agreement), n_imbalanced, n_blocks (phase blocks with votes of any kept clone), n_blocks_oriented, votes (all kept clones), votes_oriented, ref_votes, n_swapped, n_low_conf.

  • blocks: the reference orientation per block, reusable by a per-cell module: one row per piece x phase set with reference votes: piece, chrom, start, end (the piece; a molecule belongs to it when its atom start is in [start, end)), ps (phase set of the votes table), ref (reference clone), nA_ref, nB_ref and sign (+1: phase-set haplotype A is cn_a; -1: haplotype B is cn_a; 0: tie, unoriented). Blocks absent from the table are unoriented. A cell's oriented votes on a piece are a = sum(sign > 0 ? nA : nB), b = sum(sign > 0 ? nB : nA) over its blocks with sign != 0; a / (a + b) estimates cn_a / (cn_a + cn_b) (attenuated).

  • params: use, near, chain, min_link.

Details

Chaining (chain): which haplotype of a piece is called "a" is arbitrary (only the relation between clones is measured), but MEDICC2 counts an event over adjacent pieces once only when the label is continuous. Walking along each chromosome, a piece's labels are flipped as a whole (cn_a <-> cn_b in every clone, f -> 1 - f, block signs negated) when, relative to the previous piece, (parsimony) more confidently oriented clones (ok / ref) change direction (sign of cn_a - cn_b) than keep it (clones in the same state in both pieces count 1, others 0.5), or (phase) the phase sets shared by the two pieces say that the previous piece's cn_a haplotype is this piece's cn_b (sum over shared blocks of the product of the two reference signs, weighted by min(|nA_ref - nB_ref|); used when the weights sum to >= min_link votes). The other rule is the fallback when the first has no evidence. parsimony is the default: a single long phase block straddling a piece boundary with a phase switch inside it can link the two halves of one clonal loss with opposite labels. Pieces after a chromosome start or next to a piece without imbalanced clones are not chained. Flipping never changes which clones share a haplotype within a piece.

Cells pooled per clone (use): confident (default) takes the cells confidently assigned to the clone (posterior at least min_post, not doublet-like), close to the pseudobulk members that produced the clone states, without the mixed / uncertain cells whose votes would pull f towards 0.5; assigned takes the assigned column. The reference clone orients its blocks with its own votes, so its own f is biased upwards (sign reliable, magnitude not; is_ref marks these rows). Orientation errors of the reference on blocks with few votes attenuate the other clones' f towards 0.5 but do not flip it; a clone whose oriented f is within near of 0.5 despite an imbalanced state is flagged low_conf (its cn_a / cn_b assignment is a guess).
